title: LAPLEX: The FFT of Learnable Laplace Kernels
claim: Our structured operator scales to vastly larger sizes than dense layers while staying within a modest constant factor of the fastest fixed-geometry transform.
layout: Single log-log line plot, legend on top, red dots mark memory limits
description: A single log-log line chart of runtime in milliseconds (y-axis, 10^-2 to 10^3) against the number of elements n (x-axis, 2^9 to about 2^31). A three-row legend sits above the plot. Blue lines are LAPLEX, orange lines are Dense, and green lines are cuFFT. Solid lines are the H100 and dashed lines are the RTX 2080 Ti. Shaded bands show standard deviation. Red filled dots mark the last size that fits in memory on the H100. Dashed red circles mark the same limit on the RTX 2080 Ti. The orange Dense curves rise steeply and stop early, near 2^14 to 2^16. The blue LAPLEX curves stay flat and then rise roughly linearly out to about 2^27 to 2^29. The green cuFFT curves are lowest and extend furthest, to about 2^31. The eye goes first to the red end markers.
caption: Runtime of Laplex, Dense, and torch.fft (cuFFT) versus the number of elements $n$ (log\textsubscript{2} scale) on NVIDIA H100 (solid) and RTX 2080 Ti (11\,GB; dashed). Shaded regions show standard deviation; red dots (dashed red circles for the RTX 2080 Ti) mark the last size that fits in GPU memory. Laplex scales efficiently to large $n$, cuFFT is consistently fastest, while Dense runs out of memory at relatively small sizes.
abstract: Fast matrix--vector multiplication in deep learning usually comes with a choice: fixed geometry and exact computation, as in the fast Fourier transform (FFT), or adaptive geometry paid for by dense parameters, random features, or low-rank surrogates. To move beyond this trade-off, we introduce LAPLEX, a class of exact, trainable (phased) Laplace-kernel operators. A LAPLEX layer is a typically full-rank dense matrix, implicitly defined by learnable coordinate anchors, with FFT-like scaling. Consequently, it supports trainable matrix-vector operations at vector dimensions up to $10^9$ on modern GPUs. As a neural layer, it yields compact projections and classification heads interpretable as soft, trainable routing models. The same primitive also serves as an efficient Gram operator, enabling high-dimensional covariance models on flattened images of dimension $3 \cdot 10^6$ that preserve visible spatial structure without imposing convolutional bias. These applications reflect a single principle: dense geometry can be learned without storing a dense matrix, which enables data-adaptive global interactions in regimes where ordinary dense layers are out of reach. In this sense, LAPLEX separates expressivity from storage cost: it behaves like a dense trainable matrix, but is represented and applied through a small structured set of parameters. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/laplex.
